evidence.target: candidate Animatic in Brave WebGL2 at 1600x1000
evidence.summary: The 16.17-second playback completed and observed the five shot IDs in authored order; no blackout element, console error, page error or failed request was present.
All frames have zero roll and zero occlusion; the camera remains outside the product, frame-to-frame motion is bounded, every chapter ends with a 24-frame hold, and frames 408–479 are stable.

Every screenshot was viewed. The whole product remains the spatial anchor while the axial mechanism, cascade core and six semantic systems become progressively legible; the graphite, steel and copper palette and quiet type remain coherent across the sequence.
The decoded 1600x1000 product poster remained visible at opacity 1 during loading and changed to opacity 0 only after the runtime reported ready.
The page identifies the DN80 CL2500 pneumatic cascade assembly and explicitly says structural highlighting does not simulate fluid, pressure drop or performance.

evidence.target: Brave WebGL2 on NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 / D3D11
evidence.summary: The observed run recorded a 908,680-byte model transfer, p50 16.6 ms, p95 16.8 ms and no frame over 33.3 ms; this is a local diagnostic, not a universal frame-rate guarantee.

promotion_candidates.proposed_invariant: Every product-story chapter transition must preserve a visible spatial anchor, use zero blackout and zero hidden cut, and keep camera roll at zero unless a separately approved creative route requires otherwise.
promotion_candidates.rationale: The previous delivered version made viewers dizzy; the invariant is consumer-visible, deterministic and directly testable across canonical frames and full playback.
promotion_candidates.suggested_probe: Reuse the zero-occlusion, zero-roll, bounded-step, shot-order and full-playback checks in scripts/validate_control_valve_animatic.py.
